'''John Arthur Dossey''' (March 15, 1944 – February 5, 2024) was an American [[mathematician]].

== Life and career ==
Dossey was born in [[Decatur, Illinois]], the son of Arthur<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/75847292/|title=Arthur Dossey|work=[[The Pantagraph]]|location=[[Bloomington, Illinois]]|date=May 16, 1997|access-date=August 3, 2025|page=24|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Closed access}}</ref> and Mary Dossey. He attended [[Illinois State University]], earning his [[Bachelor of Science|BS degree]] in 1965 and his [[Master of Science|MS degree]] in 1968. He also attended the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign|University of Illinois]], earning his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD degree]] in [[mathematics education]] in 1971.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/pantagraph/name/john-dossey-obituary?id=54348939|title=John Dossey Obituary (1944-2024)|work=[[The Pantagraph]]|date=February 12, 2024|access-date=August 3, 2025|via=[[Legacy.com]]}}</ref>

Dossey served as a professor in the department of [[mathematics]] at Illinois State University from 1971 to 1999. During his years as a professor, in 1989, he was named a [[distinguished professor]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.illinoisstate.edu/2024/02/in-memory-of-john-dossey/|title=In memory of John Dossey|work=[[Illinois State University]]|date=February 14, 2024|access-date=August 3, 2025}}</ref> and was awarded the [[National Council of Teachers of Mathematics|NCTM Lifetime Achievement Award]] in 1996.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nctm.org/News-and-Calendar/News/NCTM-News-Releases/In-Memoriam_-John-A_-Dossey/|title=In Memoriam: John A. Dossey|work=[[National Council of Teachers of Mathematics]]|access-date=August 3, 2025}}</ref>

== Death ==
Dossey died on February 5, 2024, in [[Tucson, Arizona]], at the age of 79.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pjstar.com/obituaries/pils0717620|title=John Arthur Dossey|work=[[Journal Star (Peoria)|Journal Star]]|date=February 10, 2024|access-date=August 3, 2025}}</ref>
